children: U.K. PMI data shows price pressures strengthened in September, which will worry Bank of England policymakers and boost the case for interest-rate hikes, RSM U.K.'s Thomas Pugh says in a note. The input and output prices balances both rose to three-month highs, the PMI data show. The outlook looks even more challenging, as rising energy prices risk pushing inflation above 4% early next year, he says. That will squeeze households' real incomes and potentially force the BOE to hike rates later this year, Pugh notes. Tax rises at the government budget announcement next month could weigh on growth too. "The next six months are likely to feel like a return to stagflation as inflation rises and growth slows," he says. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)
